paper.title_en: Towards First Detection of the Solar MSW Transition With JUNO
paper.abstract_en: Matter-induced neutrino flavor mixing (the Mikheyev-Smirnov-Wolfenstein, or MSW, effect) is a central prediction of the neutrino mixing framework, but it has not been conclusively observed. Direct observation of the energy-dependent MSW transition in the solar electron-neutrino survival probability would solve this, but backgrounds have been prohibitive. We show that our new technique for suppressing muon-induced spallation backgrounds will allow JUNO to measure the MSW transition at $>$4$σ$ significance in 10 years. This would strongly support upcoming multi-\$1B next-generation experiments and their goals in cementing the neutrino mixing framework.
